obligation: FedRAMP Initial Incident Report (Class C: FR-1 and FR-2 today)
citation: FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026: IEC-CSO-EFR; IEC-CSO-DPR; IEC-CSO-IIR
trigger: A FedRAMP Reportable Incident: an incident that affects, or is likely to affect, the confidentiality or integrity of federal customer data. PAIN 5 is assumed unless promptly estimated
deadline: 1 hour for PAIN 3 to 5; 24 hours for PAIN 2; 1 business day for PAIN 1
notify: All affected parties: FedRAMP, affected agency customers (through each agency's incident procedure), and other necessary parties
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FR-1 (21 agencies on SL-1) and FR-2 (50 government customers on SL-2)
clock_starts: When the company identifies the incident as FedRAMP Reportable (IEC-CSO-EFR decision in the SOC case)

obligation: FedRAMP Initial Incident Report (Class D: SL-2 after the upgrade)
citation: FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026: IEC-CSO-IIR (Class D)
trigger: Same as above, for a Class D offering
deadline: 15 minutes for PAIN 3 to 5; 1 hour for PAIN 1 and 2
applies_at_this_tier: Not yet - applies once SL-2 holds Class D; drilled now (POAM-010)

trigger: A reported incident is still being handled
deadline: Class C: every 6 hours (PAIN 3 to 5), 24 hours (PAIN 2), 1 business day (PAIN 1). Class D: every 3 hours (PAIN 3 to 5), 6 hours (PAIN 2), 24 hours (PAIN 1)
notify: Same parties as the initial report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: The incident is resolved and recovery is complete
deadline: Class C: 6 hours (PAIN 3 to 5) or 1 business day (PAIN 1 and 2). Class D: 3 hours (PAIN 3 to 5), 6 hours (PAIN 2), 24 hours (PAIN 1)
notify: Same parties as the initial report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: FedRAMP sends an Emergency or Emergency Test message to the FedRAMP Security Inbox
deadline: Within the timeframe stated in the message
notify: Route to a senior security official (CISO); reply to FedRAMP
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: The company determines it has had a computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services to a bank for four or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible after that determination
notify: At least one bank-designated point of contact at each affected bank; if none was provided, the bank's CEO and CIO or two people of comparable responsibility by any reasonable means (53.4(a)(1)-(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 210 banking organizations on SL-1 and SL-3. Scheduled maintenance, testing, or updates previously communicated are excluded (53.4(b))
clock_starts: The company's determination (incident commander records the time)

obligation: Bank customers' own notice to their regulator (context)
citation: 12 CFR 53.3 (OCC) and the parallel FRB and FDIC rules
trigger: A bank determines that a notification incident has occurred
deadline: No later than 36 hours after the bank's determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the bank's duty. The company's notice and updates feed the bank's clock

obligation: DFARS cyber incident report (DIB customer flow-down)
trigger: Cyber incident that affects covered defense information stored by a DIB customer on SL-2
deadline: Rapidly report: within 72 hours of discovery
notify: Support each affected DIB customer's report to DoD (DIBNet portal) and report directly where the DFARS addendum requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 420 DIB customers on SL-2 through the DFARS addendum

trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported incident
deadline: As DoD directs
notify: DoD Cyber Crime Center (through the DIB customer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - by DFARS addendum

trigger: Cyber incident reported under (c)
deadline: Preserve images and relevant monitoring and packet capture data for at least 90 days from the report
notify: Internal hold; available to DoD on request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - by DFARS addendum (never exercised: POAM-029)
clock_starts: Submission of the cyber incident report

obligation: HIPAA business associate notice to covered entities
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI in HIPAA-eligible SL-1 services (and security incidents per the BAA)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; the BAA sets 72 hours from confirmation
notify: Each affected covered entity customer, with the identity of each affected individual when known
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 1,100 health care customers under BAAs
clock_starts: Discovery (first day known to any workforce member or agent)

trigger: Confirmed security incident affecting a customer's services or data
deadline: Without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirmation
notify: Each affected customer's designated security contact, plus the status page for service impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all customers

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the covered entity (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a customer that holds Florida residents' personal information
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determining the breach or having reason to believe it occurred
notify: Each affected customer (the covered entity), with what it needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company is a third-party agent for customers' personal information
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary)
deadline: Varies by state; many states require a service provider to notify the data owner, which then notifies residents
notify: Data owners (customers) for customer data; residents, attorneys general, and consumer reporting agencies for the company's own data, as each state requires
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - always check; apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company's own data)
trigger: Breach of personal information the company itself holds (employee records; customer contact and billing data) of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15-day extension possible on good cause given to the department, for this notice only)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the company's own personal information is involved
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (company's own data)
trigger: Breach of the company's own personal information affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (company's own data)
trigger: Company must notify more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 individuals

trigger: The company determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination; delay only if the U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant (large accelerated filer)
clock_starts: Materiality determination by the disclosure committee (not discovery)

trigger: Any severity-1 incident
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery; the company runbook sets a General Counsel brief within 12 hours and a committee meeting within 24 hours of declaration
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - lessons from the incident feed the next Item 106 disclosure

trigger: Service degraded or unavailable (for example, VMs stopped or isolated by the response)
deadline: Status page updated within 15 minutes of a confirmed customer impact (company standard); credits per SLA after the month ends
notify: All customers through the status page (hosted on Cloud provider X) and its machine-readable feed
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: FBI (IC3 or field office); CISA reporting
trigger: Compromise of a tool that reaches many customers
deadline: As early as practical; supports coordinated disclosure, indicator sharing, and OFAC mitigation if extortion follows
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended (voluntary); agencies may also report the incident to CISA under their own duties

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; the proposed size criterion would cover the company
clock_starts: n/a until a final rule takes effect

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand follows the compromise
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Only for federal contracts the company holds that include the clause; not triggered by this scenario

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Only for federal contracts the company holds that include the clause; not triggered by this scenario

citation: FAR 52.204-30; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article subject to a FASCSA order in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Only for federal contracts the company holds that include the clause; not triggered by this scenario

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Supplier incident notice to the company (inbound)
citation: Supplier contracts (STD-01.3); legacy RMM vendor addendum due 2026-10-31 (POAM-022)
trigger: A supplier detects a compromise affecting company systems or data
deadline: Tier-1 contracts: 72 hours or less; legacy RMM vendor: none until the addendum is signed
applies_at_this_tier: Track at each contract
